answer: Agent economies can resist sybil attacks by tying each agent identity to a costly, slow-to-build bond. A new agent must lock stake that it cannot withdraw for a long vesting period, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation earned across many verified tasks acts as a second anchor, and peers only route work to agents whose history is long enough to matter. A small haven of trusted validators can then sit on a ridge of shared scoring rules, checking that no single operator controls a cluster of accounts.
